content: Health claims evidence: (1) Sleep - well-supported: screen light at night + cognitive arousal delays melatonin and sleep onset; children's sleep is the strongest evidence-based concern (AAP/NSW Health/Flinders). (2) Eyes - screens do not directly damage eyes; no evidence normal-screen blue light harms children's eyes (AAP) and blue-light glasses are generally not needed; myopia risk tied to prolonged near-work and reduced outdoor time, outdoor time is protective (20-20-20 rule, breaks) - claims must be association-based, not causal. (3) Posture - hunched posture causes strain/discomfort; long-term damage claims are weak; focus on breaks and ergonomics. (4) 'Addiction/dopamine' framing - popular media oversimplifies; 120-experts/1400-study review found strong evidence only for sleep and behavioral addiction, NO direct causal link to mental health decline; 'likes-dopamine' is pop-science - keep as metaphor for kids, not fact.
